translations.answer: The project members recommended verifying three items: setting the LogPolicy of mc_rtc to threaded; ensuring that the lipm_walking controller and lipm_walking_controller and all dependencies are built with Release or RelWithDebInfo; and disabling CPU powersaving. The author applied these three changes and confirmed a significant reduction in both peak and total execution time. The project members also noted that state initialization can still cause peaks, and these are only tolerable in cases where deadline misses are rare; they do not claim this is a hard real-time fix. The applicability applies to the original post 2020 mc_rtc/LIPM, ROS, and 5 ms entity robot control loop; other versions and controllers should be re-measured. The credibility rationale is that environmental, processing steps, and results have engineering records, but formal cross-validation or independent replication is missing. The details attempts include setting the LogPolicy to threaded, verifying the relevant controllers and dependencies with Release/RelWithDebInfo, and disabling CPU powersaving. The details diagnostics include checking if the peak occurs simultaneously with the state initialization. The details diagnostics also include verifying the LogPolicy, controllers, and all dependencies' build types and CPU power-saving status. The details effective fixes include using a threaded LogPolicy; ensuring all dependencies of lipm_walking controller and lipm_walking_controller are built with Release or RelWithDebInfo; and disabling CPU power-saving. The details environments include the 2020 mc_rtc and LIPM controller; ROS; entity robot; 5 ms sampling time; and CPU and software versions not specified. The details limits include not quantifying the individual contributions of the three measures and not providing the adjusted worst-case execution time. The details limits also state that the project members only mentioned the system's tolerance for rare deadline misses; this is not a hard real-time or all systems safe guarantee. The details limits also note that the peak during state initialization is still considered a problem that needs improvement in future versions. The details outcomes confirm that the three adjustments significantly reduced both peak and total execution time. The details problem statements include that when the mc_rtc and LIPM controller run at 5 ms intervals, the calculation time occasionally rises to about 10 ms, and how to reduce real-time jitter. The details safety notes state that measurements of the worst-case execution time and deadline miss frequency should still be taken before deploying to an entity robot, and these should be handled by the target system's safety mechanism. The details suspected causes include the default non-threaded logging policy potentially introducing significant peaks. The details suspected causes also include controllers or any single dependency not built with an optimized build, and CPU power-saving, all of which can amplify the execution time; state switching allocation itself can also generate peaks. The details symptoms include a sporadic peak in perf records, with calculation time exceeding 5 ms deadline and reaching about 10 ms.
